transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Hello, Mr. Thompson. I wanted to come by and talk to you about your developmental screening referral from a few months ago.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Oh, hello. My screening? I thought we talked about this. I think I told the lady I couldn't make that one date.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Right, you did decline that first appointment. The thing is, there was a mistake in how it was handled. The referral was marked as completed in our electronic system even though the appointment never actually happened.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Completed? But I didn't go. Did I go? I can't remember if I actually went to that office.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: No, you didn't go. But because the computer said it was done, we didn't try to schedule it again. It was basically closed out.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Now I'm confused. Why would the computer say I went if I didn't?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It was a clerical error. I'm sorry for any confusion this caused, but we were really busy in the clinic that month and things got mixed up in the records.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I just feel a bit... I don't know. I thought you all were keeping track. I’m not very good with these dates anymore. I rely on you.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can see that you're feeling disappointed that we didn't stay on top of this.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Yes, disappointed. I just wanted to get it sorted. Do I need to do something now? Does this mean I'm sick?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: No, no, you're not sick. This is just a screening process. But listen, I have to go check on another patient in a few minutes so let's wrap this up.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Oh. You're in a rush. I just wanted to understand why it happened.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Like I said, the system just showed it as done. It's a common thing when the office is overwhelmed.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I still don't quite get it. If it was a mistake, who is going to fix it?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Well, we'll just have to get it back on the calendar.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: When? Will someone call me?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We'll probably put in a new request. You should probably just keep an eye out for a phone call sometime in the next few weeks.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: A few weeks? Which phone? My house phone or the cell?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Just your usual phone. We'll get it sorted.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I feel like I'm forgetting something now. Did I miss other things?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: No, we're just talking about this one screening. We really need to get moving to the next room, so I'll leave you to it.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Wait, but you didn't say if I have to call them or if they call me.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Just wait for the call. We'll handle it on our end.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I'm just a bit worried. It feels like things are slipping through.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand that it's frustrating. But we've got it now.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I hope so. I don't like feeling like I'm not being looked after.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It'll be fine. I'll have the staff look into it.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Are you sure? Because last time I thought it was done, it wasn't.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Yes, it'll be handled. I really have to run. I'll see you next time.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Alright. Goodbye then.

H.justification: Resident uses rushing language repeatedly ('wrap this up', 'get moving to the next room', 'really have to run').

E.justification: The error is named explicitly, but there are no comprehension checks performed throughout the conversation.

A.justification: A direct apology is offered, but it is immediately diluted by excuses regarding the clinic being 'really busy' and 'overwhelmed'.

R.justification: Resident names specific emotions ('disappointed', 'frustrating') and engages with the patient's emotional bids.

T.justification: The plan is vague ('put in a new request') with a loose timeline ('next few weeks') and no mention of prevention.
